Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 64, English)
A Guided Astral Journey to Patal Lok: Raja Bali, Vishnu's Narayan Roop, and the Lower Realms

Sour ce: A live, guided gr oup astral-travel (sookshma yatra) session, structurally differ ent fr om a typical teaching/Q&A session — the bulk of this transcript consists of r eal-time, call-and-r esponse descriptions fr om sangat members narrating what they per ceive during a collective guided journey to Patal Lok, interspersed with teaching fr om Bhaiya. This document is Part I of III — Knowledge Base, Q&A Pairs, and Curated Conversational Q&A.

1. Session framing: moving fr om upper lokas to lower lokas. Per this teaching, Ashaeiynn has previously conducted astral journeys to many upper lokas — Chandra Lok (Moon), Surya Lok (Sun), Mangal Lok (Mars), Kalyan Lok, Hanuman Ji Maharaj's own lok, Vaikunth, and Kailash. This session marks a shift to the lower lokas specifically to experience Bhagwan Ram's (via Vishnu's) pervasive, "sarvavyapi" (all-pervading) presence even in the realms conventionally associated with asuras (demon-kings).

2. The seven lower lokas, in descending order . Per this teaching: Atal, Vital, Sutal, Mahatal, and then Patal — with a further layer sometimes referenced below that. Each has its own ruler , but one king is described as ruling over all of them collectively: Raja Bali .

3. Who Raja Bali is. Per this teaching, Raja Bali is one of Bhagwan Vishnu's most beloved and supreme devotees ("param bhakton mein se ek"), and is described as ruling the entirety of the lower realms — not merely Patal alone, but Atal, Vital, Sutal, Mahatal, and Patal together , making him "samagra roop ke raja" (king of the complete lower -world structure).

4. The Vamana Avatar story , as r etold in this session. Per this teaching, Raja Bali worshipped Bhagwan Vishnu so devotedly that Vishnu, wishing to test him, took the small form of Vamana Avatar and asked for three paces of land. Bali, laughing at the modesty of the request, granted it. The first pace covered the earth, the second covered the sky — at which point Bali understood this was Narayan himself, and for the third pace, of fered his own head, since there was nowhere else left to place it.

5. What Bali actually asked for as a boon, and what he r eceived instead. Per this teaching, pleased with Bali's devotion, Vishnu of fered him a boon. Bali requested Vaikunth Lok (or , per the immediately preceding third-eye session referenced here, Saket Lok) — but instead was made ruler of Patal Lok, the netherworld.

6. Bali's specific condition upon being sent to Patal — why Vishnu personally dwells ther e. Per this teaching, upon learning he would rule Patal instead of Vaikunth, Bali was momentarily displeased and set a condition: if he was to remain in Patal, Vishnu himself must also dwell wherever Bali resides, and Vishnu must personally control and oversee all coming and going from that realm. Bali stated he was willing to accept the role only on this condition — Vishnu agreed, which is why Vishnu's presence is described as intimately bound to Patal Lok to this day .

7. Illustrative doha (couplet) r einfor cing surr ender over self-will. Per this teaching, referencing Tulsidas — a bird ("maina") that says "I am not" (mai na) ends up worth only "10-20"; but a goat that insists "I am" (mai) loses its head, as Kabir's own head was said to have been of fered. Similarly , Bali sought Vaikunth for himself but was sent to Patal instead ("Bali mangyo Baikunth ko, Hari pathyo Patal") — illustrating that mere human intention/wishing accomplishes nothing on its own ("sonche tatkal na hot hai"), while divine
will (Hari's) accomplishes things instantly; nothing in this journey happens by the practitioner's own wish — the practitioner is called , not self-invited.

8. How astral sight (drishti) varies by practitioner during a guided gr oup journey . Per this teaching, a practitioner who already has drishti will perceive the journey visually , much as ordinary sight works. A practitioner without visual drishti but with open bodily "chakshu" (sensory awareness/chakra sensitivity) will feel it through bodily sensation and vibration instead. A practitioner with neither visual drishti nor open bodily sensation may perceive nothing consciously at all — described as indicating some kind of blocked "portal," but this does not mean no benefit occurs.

9. The guarantee that everyone benefits r egardless of conscious per ception. Per this teaching, regardless of what a given practitioner consciously perceives, their subtle (sookshma) body is described as being called and brought along on every such collective journey , and every participant receives blessing/grace ("aashirwad") — described as a guarantee ("yeh meri guarantee hai") that no one returns "empty" from such a session.

10. Repeated visits to differ ent lokas ar e described as opening drishti over time. Per this teaching, Bhaiya notes that he has personally observed that visiting many dif ferent lokas repeatedly tends to open a practitioner's drishti and bring about darshan and grace progressively , even for those who initially perceive little or nothing.

1 1. How to see the journey "in color" rather than black-and-white. Per this teaching, ordinarily a practitioner may perceive such journeys in black-and-white; to perceive them vividly and in color (comparable to watching a movie), one should let go of over - analysis and simply watch with bhaav drishti (perception rooted in devotional feeling rather than ef fortful visual straining) — beginning with the simplest single impression and letting further details emer ge naturally as attention continues.

12. Practice guidance for the gr oup journey . Per this teaching, participants should sit with both hands open, without forcing intense focus or meditation ef fort — simply of fering prayer , placing complete trust in one's guru and devta shaktis, and allowing them to reveal the experience, including anything heard mentally during the process (which is described as not originating from the practitioner's own mind).

13. Continuous mental jaap determines how "long" or "short" the journey feels/plays out. Per this teaching, if a practitioner stops their mental (mansik) jaap partway through the guided journey , the experience becomes proportionally longer/harder for them; sustaining continuous mental jaap throughout allows the practitioner to cross realms and stages much more quickly .

14. Physical/sensory signs that the opening prayer has been accepted. Per this teaching, if a practitioner's body becomes heavy , or the practitioner feels their body's "tatva" become heavy , or vibrations/tarang arise in the body immediately upon of fering the opening prayer , this indicates the prayer has been accepted.

15. Descending sensations r eported during the journey , as a general pattern. Per this teaching (illustrated through numerous realtime sangat reports), descent into the lower lokas is commonly accompanied by: increasing pressure (especially in the head/third eye), a sensation like a sudden drop in an elevator or free-fall, waves of heat, a sense of passing through concentric rings or layers of shifting color , sweating in the palms and soles, gravity-like heaviness, and occasional nausea or dizziness — described as expected and safe, not something to be alarmed by .

16. Pr otective garments/markings given during descent. Per this teaching, some practitioners perceive being given protective coverings (described variously as a dark cloak, a small blanket-like wrap, or a golden jacket) partway through the descent, intended to help the practitioner's subtle body withstand the intensity of the lower realm's environment.

17. A special "tor ch"/marker used to identify visiting gr oups fr om Ashaeiynn. Per this teaching, one participant described seeing a distinctively-shaped torch or flame lit specifically as a signal, informing the inhabitants of that realm that visitors from Ashaeiynn were arriving that day , along with the specific etiquette/guidelines to be observed for that visit.

18. The first stop: a Vishnu Tattva shrine in Narasimha form, encounter ed befor e the main palace. Per this teaching, before reaching Raja Bali's palace, the group first encounters and is instructed to bow before a shrine housing the Vishnu Tattva in the form of

Narasimha (identified as a majestic, dark-hued form with prominent eyes and teeth) — sangat are instructed to mentally chant "Jai Siyaram" 1 1 times, of fer their mantra at this shrine's feet, and complete three circumambulations, followed by bowing to an adjacent Shivling.

19. The protective "white fluid" barrier befor e Raja Bali's main palace. Per this teaching, before reaching Raja Bali's palace directly , practitioners must cross through what is described as a protective white fluid/ener gy field, identified as Bhagwan Vishnu's own tattva. Crossing safely requires continuous jaap for the entire duration of the crossing — stopping the jaap partway through risks a burning or electric-shock-like sensation in whichever part of the body is still within the field at that moment.

20. Vishnu's Vishwar oop/Narayan Roop, glimpsed above the white fluid. Per this teaching, above this protective field, practitioners may glimpse Bhagwan Vishnu's Vishwaroop (universal form) — explicitly identified as the same form shown to Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita, here called the "Narayan Roop" — described by sangat as overwhelmingly radiant, compared to the brightness of ten suns aligned together , with its full story ("katha") known only to Narayan Bhagwan himself, not fully expressible or comprehensible to human minds.

21. Entering the main court (darbar) of Raja Bali. Per this teaching, the entrance hall is described (by multiple sangat members) as containing roughly a hundred massive pillars in a single hall, capable of seating perhaps a thousand people; numerous attendants stand along both sides of the entry path, some in armor and carrying weapons, guiding visitors inward one by one; approximately eight to ten thrones/seats are arranged around the main throne, occupied by ministers.

22. Raja Bali's thr one is described as extraordinarily tall. Per this teaching, sangat members estimated the throne's height, by comparison to ordinary human scale, at roughly six to seven feet, approached via wide steps, with the surrounding ministers' seats appearing to "float" nearby .

23. Signs of Devi Lakshmi's pr esence throughout the palace. Per this teaching, participants described sensing an intense, pervasive feeling of abundance and prosperity throughout the palace, attributed to Devi Lakshmi's flowing presence within it.

24. Raja Bali's arrival, and the specific difficulty of per ceiving his form dir ectly . Per this teaching, upon Raja Bali's arrival, practitioners reported an overwhelming brightness and intensity of ener gy — a green-glowing jewel or "naag mani" (serpent-jewel) reportedly set in his crown, accompanied by an audible hissing sound associated with a serpent; several participants and even Bhaiya himself explicitly reported being unable to make out Raja Bali's face directly due to the sheer intensity of the surrounding light, describing it as more overwhelming than even the earlier Narayan Roop darshan in this same session.

25. Bhaiya's own explicit acknowledgment of this being unpr ecedented. Per this teaching, Bhaiya states that across many prior loka visits — including visits to numerous devtas and rulers of various realms — this was the first time even he was unable to fully see a ruler's face directly , attributing this specifically to the sheer magnitude of Raja Bali's accumulated tapobal (power from austerity) and bhakti.

26. The offering/prayer protocol befor e Raja Bali. Per this teaching, participants were instructed to mentally chant "Jai Siyaram" 21 times and of fer/surrender their mantra at Raja Bali's feet, taking their guru as witness ("Gurudev ko sirodhari karke, Bhaiya ko sakshi maankar").

27. A collective bhajan/kirtan was sung during the darshan, with devtas r eportedly showering flower petals in r esponse. Per this teaching, sangat sang together (referencing the well-known Ram-stuti beginning "Mangal bhavan amangal hari, dravahu su Dashrath ajir bihari..."), and multiple participants reported perceiving flower petals being showered down from above by devtas in response to the collective devotion.

28. Gifts/symbols r eceived by practitioners during the mantra-offering. Per this teaching, various sangat members reported receiving impressions of golden boxes, a red wheel (chakra), a conch (shankh), and a general sense of a mixing/blending between their own aura and Raja Bali's aura during this of fering.

29. Bhaiya's closing declaration of Raja Bali's statur e. Per this teaching, standing symbolically in Raja Bali's own darbar , Bhaiya publicly af firms: Raja Bali is not merely the ruler of Patal alone but of Atal, Vital, Sutal, Mahatal, and Patal collectively , is among Bhagwan Vishnu's supreme devotees, and earned this stature entirely through his own bhakti and tapobal (devotional and ascetic power) — not by lesser means.

30. Why Raja Bali is described as difficult to see even for advanced practitioners. Per this teaching, Raja Bali is explicitly described as not merely "the ruler of one lok" like many other lokas visited previously (where devtas and kings were seen clearly) — his stature is described as categorically dif ferent, which is of fered as the reason his form proved so dif ficult to perceive directly even for well-established practitioners in this session.

31. Who specifically should seek Raja Bali's blessing, per this teaching. Three groups are specifically named: (1) anyone facing money/finance-related problems (connected to "Dharti Tatva"/the earth element and "Arth," meaning wealth); (2) anyone lacking patience (dhairya) or whose root (mooladhar) chakra is unstable — visiting Raja Bali is described as bringing full stability and peace to such a person; and (3) anyone specifically seeking deeper Ram bhakti, since Raja Bali is himself described as deeply devoted to Ram's name specifically , and is said to grant the boon of devotion to those who seek it from him.

32. Every dimension/element within Patal is described as intensely "awakened" (jagrit). Per this teaching, Bhaiya describes every tattva (element) within Patal — from the finest point of time itself to the full stream of knowledge — as having been fully awakened across all seven of these lower realms by Raja Bali himself, which is of fered as the reason for the intensity of everything experienced during this visit.

33. Closing of the guided journey: r eturn via bowing to Dharti Mata (Mother Earth). Per this teaching, the session concludes with participants bowing first to their Gurudev and then specifically to Dharti Mata (Mother Earth); this bow to the earth is what specifically completes the return of the subtle body back to ordinary waking awareness.

34. Practical guidance for the remainder of the day/night after this practice. Per this teaching, participants are advised that they may eat following this practice, or may choose to wait until morning if closer to nighttime — of fered as simple, practical closing guidance rather than a strict rule.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This session is a guided group astral journey (sookshma yatra) to the lower lokas (Atal, Vital, Sutal, Mahatal, Patal), ruled collectively by Raja Bali, a supreme devotee of Bhagwan Vishnu. Raja Bali's story: he of fered his own head as Vishnu's third step in the Vamana Avatar story , asked for Vaikunth/Saket Lok as a boon, but was instead made ruler of Patal — on the condition that Vishnu himself would dwell there and personally oversee it. How a practitioner experiences the journey depends on their own development: visual drishti shows it directly; open bodily sensitivity shows it as physical sensation; neither shows nothing consciously — but everyone's subtle body is called and everyone receives blessing regardless. Continuous mental jaap throughout the guided journey shortens and eases the experience; stopping it midway makes the journey feel longer and harder . A protective white-fluid barrier (V ishnu's own tattva) must be crossed via continuous jaap before reaching Raja Bali's palace — stopping mid-crossing risks a burning/shock-like sensation. Raja Bali's form proved too radiant to see directly even for Bhaiya himself in this session — described as unprecedented across all prior loka visits, attributed to the sheer magnitude of his tapobal and bhakti. Raja Bali should specifically be sought by: those with money/finance problems, those lacking patience or with an unstable root chakra, and those seeking deeper Ram bhakti. The journey concludes by bowing to Gurudev and then to Dharti Mata (Mother Earth), which completes the return to ordinary waking awareness.

This session included extensive, genuine live sangat interaction (real-time collective narration throughout the guided journey), so Part III (Curated Conversational Q&A) is included — though, given this session's distinct guided-meditation format, Part III here curates the most vivid shared-experience moments rather than a typical Q&A exchange. Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 64, English)
A Guided Astral Journey to Patal Lok: Raja Bali and Vishnu's Narayan Roop
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live guided astral-travel session. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siyaram."

This session specifically visits the lower lokas for the first time, to experience Bhagwan Ram's pervasive presence even in realms conventionally associated with asuras.

The first pace covered the earth, the second the sky , revealing Vishnu's true identity — and for the third pace, since nowhere else remained, Bali of fered his own head.
Q5. What boon did Bali ask for , and what did he actually r eceive? A: Per this teaching, Bali asked for Vaikunth Lok (or Saket Lok), but was instead made ruler of Patal Lok.

Q8. Will I actually "see" the journey if I don't alr eady have drishti? A: Per this teaching, it depends on your own development — a practitioner with visual drishti perceives the journey directly; one without visual drishti but with open bodily sensitivity perceives it through physical sensation and vibration instead; one with neither may perceive nothing consciously , though this does not mean no benefit occurs.

Q9. Does everyone benefit fr om a guided gr oup astral journey , even if they don't per ceive anything? A: Yes — per this teaching, everyone's subtle body is described as being called and brought along regardless of conscious perception, and everyone receives blessing; Bhaiya of fers this as an explicit guarantee.

Q10. How can I per ceive these journeys in color rather than black-and-white? A: Per this teaching, let go of over -analysis and watch with "bhaav drishti" (perception rooted in devotional feeling) — start with the simplest single impression and allow further
details to emer ge naturally with continued attention.

Q1 1. Does stopping mental jaap partway thr ough a guided journey have any r eal effect? A: Yes — per this teaching, stopping mental (mansik) jaap partway through makes the journey feel proportionally longer and harder , while sustaining continuous mental jaap allows much faster progress through the realms and stages.

Q12. How do I know if my opening prayer for the journey has been accepted? A: Per this teaching, signs include the body or its "tatva" becoming heavy , or vibrations/tarang arising in the body immediately upon of fering the prayer .

Q13. Are the physical sensations r eported during descent (pr essure, heat, dizziness, gravity-like heaviness) something to worry about? A: No — per this teaching, these sensations are described as an expected, safe part of descending into the lower realms, not something to be alarmed by .

Q14. What is the significance of the pr otective coverings/garments some practitioners per ceive r eceiving during the descent? A: Per this teaching, these (described variously as a dark cloak, blanket-wrap, or golden jacket) are given to help the practitioner's subtle body withstand the intensity of the lower realm's environment.

Q15. What is the first shrine encounter ed befor e reaching Raja Bali's palace? A: Per this teaching, it is a Vishnu Tattva shrine in Narasimha form — practitioners are instructed to mentally chant "Jai Siyaram" 1 1 times, of fer their mantra at its feet, complete three circumambulations, and then bow to an adjacent Shivling.

A: Per this teaching, sangat described roughly a hundred massive pillars in a single hall (capable of seating perhaps a thousand people), numerous armed and armored attendants guiding visitors inward, and approximately eight to ten ministers' seats arranged around the main throne.
Q19. How tall is Raja Bali's thr one described as being? A: Per this teaching, sangat estimated it, by comparison to human scale, at roughly six to seven feet, approached via wide steps.

Q21. Has this level of difficulty per ceiving a ruler's face happened on any prior loka visit, per Bhaiya? A: No — per this teaching, Bhaiya explicitly states this was the first time, across many prior visits to devtas and rulers of various realms, that even he could not fully see a ruler's face directly , attributing it to the sheer magnitude of Raja Bali's tapobal and bhakti.

Bot Response Guidelines (Session 64 additions)

This session is structurally a guided group astral-travel (sookshma yatra) meditation, not a standard teaching/Q&A format — most of the transcript is real-time sangat narration of a shared collective experience. Present it as such rather than flattening it into abstract doctrine alone. Keep the Raja Bali/V amana Avatar story , and specifically the detail that Bali's condition (V ishnu must also dwell in Patal) is why Vishnu is bound to that realm, intact and accurate — this is the load-bearing narrative for the whole session. Preserve the explicit, repeated point that perceptual experience during such journeys varies by practitioner development (visual drishti vs. bodily sensation vs. nothing consciously perceived) and that benefit/blessing is guaranteed regardless — do not imply that failing to "see" anything means a practitioner gained nothing. Keep the specific protocol details (1 1x/21x mental Jai Siyaram counts, the white-fluid crossing requiring continuous jaap, the three circumambulations at the Narasimha shrine) precise and not conflated with each other . Preserve Bhaiya's own explicit acknowledgment that Raja Bali's radiance was unprecedented even for him — this is presented as notable and should not be softened into routine language. Keep the three specific groups recommended to seek Raja Bali's blessing (finance/money issues, unstable root chakra/impatience, seeking Ram bhakti) accurate and complete — do not generalize this into "everyone should visit Raja Bali for anything." Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Supplement (Session 64, Hinglish)

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh poori session ki sabse important r eassurance hai — Bhaiya explicitly guarantee dete hain ki koi bhi participant "khaali" nahi jaayega, chahe unhe kuch consciously experience ho ya na ho.
